lines.raw: Generic. Fills: 8,640. Gross amount: $216,000. Members paid: $43,200. Plan paid: $172,800. Share of plan paid: 18.0%.
lines.say: Generic. Fills: 8,640. Gross amount: 216000 dollars. Members paid: 43200 dollars. Plan paid: 172800 dollars. Share of plan paid: 18.0 percent.

lines.raw: Brand (not specialty). Fills: 900. Gross amount: $540,000. Members paid: $36,000. Plan paid: $504,000. Share of plan paid: 52.4%.
lines.say: Brand (not specialty). Fills: 900. Gross amount: 540000 dollars. Members paid: 36000 dollars. Plan paid: 504000 dollars. Share of plan paid: 52.4 percent.

lines.say: Specialty (all brand). Fills: 60. Gross amount: 300000 dollars. Members paid: 15000 dollars. Plan paid: 285000 dollars. Share of plan paid: 29.6 percent.

lines.raw: **Total**. Fills: **9,600**. Gross amount: **$1,056,000**. Members paid: **$94,200**. Plan paid: **$961,800**. Share of plan paid: **100%**.
lines.say: Total. Fills: 9,600. Gross amount: 1056000 dollars. Members paid: 94200 dollars. Plan paid: 961800 dollars. Share of plan paid: 100 percent.

lines.raw: Each row: gross = members paid + plan paid.

Specialty: 15000 dollars and 285000 dollars = 300000 dollars ✓.

lines.raw: Bluebonnet had on average **1,000 members** (employees and family) covered for the whole year: 1,000 × 12 = **12,000 member months** (one member covered for one month = one member month; covered in the Eligibility course).

lines.raw: Step 2: the key measures.
lines.say: Step 2: the key measures.

lines.raw: Per member per month (PMPM) drug spend.
lines.say: Per member per month (P M P M) drug spend.

lines.raw: PMPM equals Plan paid ÷ Member months.
lines.say: P M P M equals Plan paid ÷ Member months.

lines.raw: For example: $961,800 ÷ 12,000 equals $80.15 PMPM plan paid.
lines.say: For example: 961800 dollars ÷ 12,000 equals 80 dollars 15 cents P M P M plan paid.

lines.raw: Gross (plan plus members): $1,056,000 ÷ 12,000 equals $88.00 PMPM.
lines.say: Gross (plan plus members): 1056000 dollars ÷ 12,000 equals 88 dollars P M P M.

lines.raw: Generic dispensing rate (GDR).
lines.say: Generic dispensing rate (G D R).

lines.raw: GDR equals Generic fills ÷ All fills.
lines.say: G D R equals Generic fills ÷ All fills.

lines.raw: For example: 8,640 ÷ 9,600 equals 90.0%.
lines.say: For example: 8,640 ÷ 9,600 equals 90.0 percent.

lines.raw: Fills per member per year.
lines.say: Fills per member per year.

lines.raw: Fills ÷ Average members.
lines.say: Fills ÷ Average members.

lines.raw: For example: 9,600 ÷ 1,000 equals 9.6 fills per member per year.
lines.say: For example: 9,600 ÷ 1,000 equals 9.6 fills per member per year.

lines.raw: What the summary tells the consultant.
lines.say: What the summary tells the consultant.

lines.raw: Generics are most fills but little money. Numbers: 90.0% of fills, 18.0% of plan paid. Why it matters: Generic prices (MAC, any spread) matter, but small savings per fill.
lines.say: Generics are most fills but little money. Numbers: 90.0 percent of fills, 18.0 percent of plan paid. Why it matters: Generic prices (M A C, any spread) matter, but small savings per fill.

lines.raw: Brands are the biggest cost. Numbers: 9.4% of fills, 52.4% of plan paid. Why it matters: Rebates matter most here (lesson 2).
lines.say: Brands are the biggest cost. Numbers: 9.4 percent of fills, 52.4 percent of plan paid. Why it matters: Rebates matter most here (lesson 2).

lines.raw: Specialty is tiny in count, huge in cost. Numbers: 60 fills (0.6%), 29.6% of plan paid. Why it matters: A handful of members drive a large share. Specialty pricing and programs matter.
lines.say: Specialty is tiny in count, huge in cost. Numbers: 60 fills (0.6 percent), 29.6 percent of plan paid. Why it matters: A handful of members drive a large share. Specialty pricing and programs matter.

lines.say: Where is Emily?

lines.say: In 2025 Emily had 6 generic fills: amoxicillin for strep throat in March, ibuprofen after her appendix surgery in June, and four fills of atorvastatin for cholesterol from July (the last a 90-day mail-order fill).

lines.raw: Step 3: rebates per claim.
lines.say: Step 3: rebates per claim.

lines.raw: Both PBMs expect rebates of about **$200 per brand fill** (brand and specialty together: 900 + 60 = **960 fills**).
lines.say: Both P B M's expect rebates of about 200 dollars per brand fill (brand and specialty together: 900 and 60 = 960 fills).

lines.raw: Here is a quick table.
lines.say: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: Expected rebates. Calculation: 960 brand fills × $200. Result: **$192,000**.
lines.say: Expected rebates. Calculation: 960 brand fills × 200 dollars. Result: 192000 dollars.

lines.raw: Rebates per brand claim. Calculation: $192,000 ÷ 960. Result: $200.00.
lines.say: Rebates per brand claim. Calculation: 192000 dollars ÷ 960. Result: 200 dollars.

lines.raw: Rebates per claim (all fills). Calculation: $192,000 ÷ 9,600. Result: **$20.00**.
lines.say: Rebates per claim (all fills). Calculation: 192000 dollars ÷ 9,600. Result: 20 dollars.

lines.raw: Rebates PMPM. Calculation: $192,000 ÷ 12,000. Result: $16.00.
lines.say: Rebates P M P M. Calculation: 192000 dollars ÷ 12,000. Result: 16 dollars.

lines.raw: Always say "per what".
lines.say: Always say "per what".

lines.raw: "$200 per claim" and "$20 per claim" can describe the **same** rebates: one divides by brand claims, the other by all claims.
lines.say: "200 dollars per claim" and "20 dollars per claim" can describe the same rebates: one divides by brand claims, the other by all claims.

lines.raw: When comparing PBM offers, make sure both use the same denominator.
lines.say: When comparing P B M offers, make sure both use the same denominator.

lines.raw: + Spread on generics. Calculation: A: 8,640 × $3.00. PBM A: traditional: $25,920. PBM B: pass-through: $0.
lines.say: + Spread on generics. Calculation: A: 8,640 × 3 dollars. P B M A: traditional: 25920 dollars. P B M B: pass-through: 0 dollars.

lines.raw: + Admin fees. Calculation: B: 9,600 × $3.00. PBM A: traditional: $0. PBM B: pass-through: $28,800.
lines.say: + Admin fees. Calculation: B: 9,600 × 3 dollars. P B M A: traditional: 0 dollars. P B M B: pass-through: 28800 dollars.

lines.raw: − Rebates received. Calculation: A: 80% of $192,000. B: 100%. PBM A: traditional: − $153,600. PBM B: pass-through: − $192,000.
lines.say: − Rebates received. Calculation: A: 80 percent of 192000 dollars. B: 100 percent. P B M A: traditional: − 153600 dollars. P B M B: pass-through: − 192000 dollars.

lines.raw: **Net cost to Bluebonnet**. PBM A: traditional: **$834,120**. PBM B: pass-through: **$798,600**.
lines.say: Net cost to Bluebonnet. P B M A: traditional: 834120 dollars. P B M B: pass-through: 798600 dollars.

lines.raw: **Net PMPM**. Calculation: ÷ 12,000 member months. PBM A: traditional: **$69.51**. PBM B: pass-through: **$66.55**.
lines.say: Net P M P M. Calculation: ÷ 12,000 member months. P B M A: traditional: 69 dollars 51 cents. P B M B: pass-through: 66 dollars 55 cents.

lines.raw: PBM earns from Bluebonnet. Calculation: A: $25,920 spread + $38,400 retained rebates. PBM A: traditional: $64,320. PBM B: pass-through: $28,800.
lines.say: P B M earns from Bluebonnet. Calculation: A: 25920 dollars spread and 38400 dollars retained rebates. P B M A: traditional: 64320 dollars. P B M B: pass-through: 28800 dollars.

lines.raw: Check the maths.
lines.say: Check the maths.
A: 961800 dollars and 25920 dollars − 153600 dollars = 834120 dollars ✓.
B: 961800 dollars and 28800 dollars − 192000 dollars = 798600 dollars ✓.
Difference: 834120 dollars − 798600 dollars = 35520 dollars a year, or 69 dollars 51 cents − 66 dollars 55 cents = 2 dollars 96 cents P M P M.

lines.raw: Retained rebates under A: $192,000 − $153,600 = $38,400 ✓.
lines.say: Retained rebates under A: 192000 dollars − 153600 dollars = 38400 dollars ✓.

lines.raw: Change one term and the answer can flip.
lines.say: Change one term and the answer can flip.

lines.raw: Suppose PBM A agreed to pass on **100%** of rebates but kept its $3.00 generic spread: $961,800 + $25,920 − $192,000 = **$795,720**, which is **$2,880 cheaper** than PBM B.
lines.say: Suppose P B M A agreed to pass on 100 percent of rebates but kept its 3 dollars generic spread: 961800 dollars and 25920 dollars − 192000 dollars = 795720 dollars which is 2880 dollars cheaper than P B M B.
